sentences.text: This i s first application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of the applicant who has been arrested relating to FIR/Crime No.953/2022 dated 12.10.2022 registered at Police Station Sarai, District Singrauli for the offences punishable under Section 302 of IPC.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in custody since 12.10.2022.
He further submits that applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case and trial will take considerable time to be concluded.
He further submits that applicant is a permanent resident of district and is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the conditions to be imposed by the Court.

Upon these Rajkumar @ Raju Prajapati vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164652238/
1 grounds, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
The prosecution case is that the dead body of the wife of applicant was found lying in the room situated in the agricultural field of the applicant.
The room was locked from outside.
The bail application is argued on the point that there were serious marital dispute between the deceased and applicant.

As is evident from the fact that not only a case for maintenance was filed by the deceased against the applicant but she had also filed one complaint case under Section 494 of IPC and a criminal case was also registered under Section 498A of IPC at the behest of deceased.
It is argued forcefully that in a condition of such strained relationship why would deceased have come to live with the applicant.
For this, the statements of witnesses have been recorded during investigation.

Radhika is the second wife of the applicant who has disclosed that a compromise was arrived at in the month of June, 2022 wherein it was agreed that the first wife namely, Archana and also the witness Radhika will live with the applicant as his wives.
Similarly relative of the deceased Ram Bahore has disclosed that three days prior to the incident, the applicant had taken the deceased along with him to the place where she was later found dead.
In the light of these strong circumstantial evidence, this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the applicant.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands dismissed.

(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE Nitesh Rajkumar @ Raju Prajapati vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164652238/
